claim.title: Critical exponent in 1D exponential model
claim.statement: In the 1D exponential model, the test error $E(t)$ near the grokking transition time $t_\epsilon$ scales as $E(t) \propto (t_\epsilon - t)^1$, indicating a critical exponent of 1.
claim.test_plan: Simulate the 1D exponential model described in Section 3.2. Sample $N$ positive and $N$ negative samples from $P^+(x) = e^{-(x-\epsilon)}\Theta(x-\epsilon)$ and $P^-(x) = e^{-(\epsilon-x)}\Theta(\epsilon-x)$ with a shift to induce grokking (as in Fig 3). Train a perceptron $f(x)=\text{sgn}(x-b)$ using gradient descent on the loss $R = \frac{1}{2N}\sum \frac{1}{2}(\hat{y}_i - y_i)^2 + \frac{\lambda_2}{2}b^2 + \lambda_1|w|$. Record the test error $E(t)$ for $t < t_\epsilon$. Fit the log-log plot of $E(t)$ vs $(t_\epsilon - t)$ to a power law $E(t) = A(t_\epsilon - t)^\nu$. Pass if the fitted exponent $\nu$ is within 0.05 of 1.0.
claim.evidence_in_paper: Section 3.2.1, Eq. 9 and 10: 'Grokking in the considered 1D exponential model is a second-order phase transition with the test-error critical exponent equal to one.'
claim.success_criterion: The fitted critical exponent $\nu$ from the log-log slope of test error vs time-to-transition is $1.0 \pm 0.05$.
